decisions.statement: A manifest parted from its lockfile refuses every install of the whole tree.
A landing with no manifest is left alone without the lockfile being read.
A manifest is a file named `package.json` at the root or under a folder.
A manifest arriving and a manifest going are the same event here.
A landing with a lockfile of its own is taken at its word.
The lockfile is made from the manifests the base commit tracks.
The manifests a landing carries are worked into that set before the making.
The lockfile is made with the worktree read for nothing.
The making happens in a scratch tree swept however the making ends.
A lockfile the making leaves unchanged is carried by no landing.
The lockfile made is answered as a change rather than as a body.
A base commit tracking no lockfile is answered an addition rather than a replacement.
A lockfile that could not be made leaves the landing whole and says so.
A row appending states no manifest.
Nothing here refuses a landing.
Nothing here commits.
An install points the workspace at the folders its manifests name.
A landing with a manifest installs the checkout onto the commit that landing landed.
A landing with no manifest installs nothing.
The install runs once the landing has given up the hold.
Two landings with a manifest at once install at once.
A failed install leaves the commit made and says the tree reaches nothing until that install runs.
A lockfile the install makes again says the commit has a lockfile its manifests do not warrant.
An install takes away a link under `node_modules` reaching a folder no manifest names.
A link inside a folder under `node_modules` is reached as a link directly under `node_modules` is.
The folder with a link is reached whether or not the folder names a scope.
No link deeper than one folder below `node_modules` is reached.
A link reaching the folder whose manifest names that link is left alone.
A link reaching a folder whose manifest names another package is taken away.
A folder under `node_modules` that is no link is left alone.
The links an install took away are said alongside the install.
A landing whose lockfile could not be made is answered for by the audit.
A manifest moved from one path to another is a manifest going and a manifest arriving.
A manifest a rename names is read from the array an edit's manifest is read from.
A manifest moved is renamed in the scratch tree before the manifests are worked in.
A landing moving a manifest to another path is a landing with a manifest.

definition: the lockfile a landing's manifests warrant, and the install pointing the workspace at them
